rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Delegation recognized: 18:19 ('send one of you with this silver coin') and 12:55 (Yusuf: 'appoint me over the storehouses'). Root w-k-l.
rows.detail_long: The sleepers of the cave appointing one to buy food, and Yusuf requesting stewardship of Egypt's stores — the Qur'an's two delegation scenes that jurists build agency on.

rows.display_note: Shown at 610 CE; app dating range 610–700 CE, confidence low
rows.name: Sunan Abi Da'ud 3625

topics_app: The Office of the Judge (Kitab Al-Aqdiyah)

rows.detail: The Prophet appointed agents: Urwah al-Bariqi to buy a sacrificial animal, agents to collect zakat, Jabir at Khaybar — app grading Da'eef, app dating 610-700 low.
rows.detail_long: The appointment reports establish agency by prophetic practice. Note honestly: the app's file grades this particular narration Da'eef and dates it broadly (610-700, low confidence); the Urwah al-Bariqi report also runs in Bukhari, Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah through stronger chains.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2311
rows.detail: Deputed to guard the sadaqa. 'Allah's Messenger deputed me to keep the Sadaqat of Ramadan' — custody agency over public alms, with the agent answerable to the principal.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: Abu Hurairah is appointed keeper of the zakat al-fitr stores, catches a night thief, and threatens to bring him to the Prophet — the agent enforcing on the principal's authority. Agency over other people's property, with accountability running back to the appointer.
rows.evidence_display: Sahih Bukhari 2311 (text + grading + dating block in app)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632 (Madinan), displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.display_note: Agency named explicitly — 'appointed a man as an agent in Khaybar' — and the principal corrects the agent's dealings
rows.name: Muwatta 1368

hadith_meta.narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayra

rows.detail: The agent at Khaybar, supervised. The Prophet appoints an agent over Khaybar; when the agent swaps dates unequally, the principal audits and corrects the transaction.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: 'the Messenger of Allah... appointed a man as an agent in Khaybar, and he brought him some excellent dates' — obtained, it emerges, at one-for-two. The exchange is corrected on the spot (the like-for-like rule). The principal remains responsible for HOW the agent transacts: agency does not launder a defective deal.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch5_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632 (Madinan), displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.name: Mishkat al-Masabih 1384

hadith_meta.narrator: (on) Ali; Abu Dawud transmitted it, Tirmidhi similar

rows.detail: Sacrifice performed on his behalf. Ali, sacrificing two rams: 'God's Messenger enjoined me to sacrifice on his behalf, so that is what I am doing' — delegation even in acts of worship with property.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: agency's widest reach — a ritual act involving property (the sacrifice) validly performed by a deputy on the principal's instruction, continuing after the principal's death. The doctrinal anchor for the rule that whatever a person may do himself, he may in principle appoint another to do.
rows.evidence_display: Mishkat al-Masabih 1384 (text + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch5_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 18:19 — the Cave companions 'send one of you with this money to the city': one purse, one deputed buyer.
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on 18:19 names the actors: the chief proposes and Yamlikha (Yamblichus) is sent 'with this money' to buy food for the group — one member deputed to transact with common funds for all. The verse classical jurists cite as the Qur'anic picture of wakala. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q18:19 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch5_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Qurtubi
rows.detail: Al-Qurtubi reads 'send/appoint' (ib'athu) in 18:19 as a basis for agency.
rows.detail_long: Al-Qurtubi on 18:19 (app file) reads the cave-sleepers' 'send one of you with this silver coin to the city' as delegation — one acting for the group with their money — the agency seed the fiqh manuals grow into wakala.
rows.evidence_display: al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an, on Q18:19 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Ibn Rushd
rows.detail: Ibn Rushd lists the four pillars of agency: principal, agent, subject matter, formula.
rows.detail_long: Bidayat's compact treatment fixes the structural anatomy of wakala the schools share. App book F0751-B51.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.5; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
rows.detail: Al-Mughni (5:71) treats agency including the fuduli — the unauthorized agent awaiting ratification.
rows.detail_long: Ibn Qudama covers appointment, scope and the fuduli doctrine; al-Kasani's Bada'i does the same for the Hanafis. App book F0749-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.5; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted Shari'ah Board meeting 14, Dubai, 21-22 Rabi' I 1426 / 30 April-2 May 2005
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 23 (Agency), adopted 2005. Investment agency becomes the workhorse of deposits, sukuk and takaful.
rows.detail_long: SS23 codifies wakalah bi'l-istithmar — the fee-based investment agency now carrying more sukuk volume than any other structure. VERIFIED: adopted 2 May 2005 (not 2002). VERIFIED THIS SESSION (SS23 full text, ss2.txt): adoption 30 April - 2 May 2005, Dubai (meeting 14). CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT: 3/1 agency is immediate by default (effective on conclusion; conditional and future-effective forms exist); 4/1/1 general agency covers all disposal methods within the principal's interest and customary practice; 4/2/2 PAID agency falls under the ijarah rulings; 4/2/3 remuneration must be known — lump sum or a share of a specified income; 5/1/1 in procurement agency the principal bears the price and reimburses the agent's expenses; 6/1/1 the agent's deals with close relatives are permissible unless collusion against the principal's interest appears.
rows.internal_ref: Verified from the official AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards 2015 full text (user-supplied PDF, adoption page read this session) | SS23 adoption + clauses read verbatim from ss2.txt (2026-07-14)

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: The single largest sukuk structure: 27.3% of 2022 issuance (IFSB 2023).
rows.detail_long: Investment agency out-grew the profit-sharing contracts it was meant to serve — fee certainty beat profit-share uncertainty in practice.
